blocks.text: JavaScript has seven primitive types; everything else is an object. Primitives are immutable and compared by value; objects are compared by reference.
typeof null === 'object' is a bug kept for backward compatibility. Check null with value === null. Also, typeof on an array returns 'object'; use Array.isArray(value).
There is one number type for integers and decimals: a 64-bit IEEE-754 floating-point double. That explains most number surprises.

blocks.code:
0.1 + 0.2 === 0.3;                          // false (0.30000000000000004)
Math.abs(0.1 + 0.2 - 0.3) < Number.EPSILON; // true: compare with a tolerance

Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;        // 9007199254740991 (2^53 - 1)
9007199254740992 === 9007199254740993; // true: precision lost

10 / 0;      // Infinity (no error)
'abc' * 2;   // NaN ("Not a Number" is of type number)
NaN === NaN; // false: the only value not equal to itself
Number.isNaN(NaN);   // true
isNaN('abc');        // true: global isNaN coerces first, avoid it

blocks.text: For money, store integer cents (1999 instead of 19.99) or use a decimal library. Use BigInt (123n) for integers beyond 2^53.

blocks.code:
const first = 'Ada';
const greeting = `Hello, ${first}! 2 + 2 = ${2 + 2}`; // template literal
const multi = `line 1
line 2`;                                        // real newlines allowed

const s = 'cat';
s[0] = 'b';          // silently ignored: strings are immutable
s.toUpperCase();     // returns a NEW string 'CAT'; s is still 'cat'

'😀'.length;          // 2: length counts UTF-16 code units, not characters
[...'😀'].length;     // 1

blocks.text: Conditions accept any value and convert it to a boolean. Only eight values are falsy; everything else, including every object and array, is truthy.

blocks.code:
Boolean('');     // false
Boolean('0');    // true
Boolean([]);     // true
!!'hello';       // true: double negation converts to boolean

blocks.text: undefined means "no value was ever assigned": uninitialized variables, missing function arguments, missing object properties, functions without return. null is an intentional "empty" set by a programmer. JSON has null but no undefined, so undefined properties disappear in JSON.stringify.
